hello. i have a question. so to my understanding the game / world is rendered on the gpu. but this log kinda conflicts that idea, that or my understanding of it is shallow. [paint] LIVE FOLIAGE PREVIEW GREW: bush → 131072 rows (6 MiB CPU) — elastic budget, the machine is the wall (req_2843)
[paint] LIVE FOLIAGE PREVIEW GREW: bush → 262144 rows (12 MiB CPU) — elastic budget, the machine is the wall (req_2843)
[paint] LIVE FOLIAGE PREVIEW GREW: bush → 524288 rows (24 MiB CPU) — elastic budget, the machine is the wall (req_2843)
[paint] LIVE FOLIAGE PREVIEW GREW: bush → 1048576 rows (48 MiB CPU) — elastic budget, the machine is the wall (req_2843)
resolution: Question, not a build ask: user saw '[paint] LIVE FOLIAGE PREVIEW GREW ... MiB CPU' and wondered if it contradicts GPU rendering. Answered from source: world_loader.zig pushFoliageRow builds 12-float per-instance rows in a CPU-side staging buffer (RAM), which is uploaded to the GPU instance pool (gpu/3d.zig growStaticPool logs the matching '[r3d] pool GREW ... device is the wall'). Rendering stays fully on GPU; the 'CPU' MiB is instance-data authoring memory for the live paint preview, deliberately labeled to distinguish it from VRAM. No code changed.
